quests.question: She burst into tears ____ she heard the wonderful news.
quests.sentence: She burst into tears ____ she heard the wonderful news.
quests.hint: Hearing the news was the specific single moment that triggered the tears.
quests.explanation: 'When' marks a specific moment that triggers an immediate reaction. The tears came at the exact moment of hearing the news. 'While' would suggest the crying happened over an extended period of listening, which is less precise.

quests.question: He was reading the news on his phone ____ his wife was preparing dinner.
quests.sentence: He was reading the news on his phone ____ his wife was preparing dinner.
quests.hint: Both activities were happening at the same time in the same household.
quests.explanation: 'While' connects two simultaneous, ongoing activities. He was reading (one ongoing action) while she was preparing dinner (another ongoing action) - both happened over the same period of time.

quests.question: She smiled warmly ____ she walked out onto the stage.
quests.sentence: She smiled warmly ____ she walked out onto the stage.
quests.hint: The smile and the walking happened at the very same instant.
quests.explanation: 'As' is used for two actions that happen at precisely the same moment - especially brief, simultaneous actions. 'As she walked onto the stage' captures the exact simultaneity of the smile and the movement.

quests.question: ____ he waited for his connecting flight, he read a few pages of his novel.
quests.sentence: ____ he waited for his connecting flight, he read a few pages of his novel.
quests.hint: Both the waiting and the reading happened during the same period.
quests.explanation: 'While' shows two simultaneous activities happening over the same period. The waiting (background condition) and the reading (foreground activity) both happened during the same stretch of time at the airport.

quests.question: He always shakes hands formally ____ he meets a new business contact.
quests.sentence: He always shakes hands formally ____ he meets a new business contact.
quests.hint: Meeting a new contact is the regular trigger for a handshake.
quests.explanation: 'When' describes a habitual action triggered by a specific event. Every time he meets someone new (trigger), he shakes hands (response). This happens consistently - 'while' would suggest the handshake is ongoing.

quests.question: Please do exactly ____ the instructions say and don't try to improvise.
quests.sentence: Please do exactly ____ the instructions say and don't try to improvise.
quests.hint: Following instructions means doing things in the way they say to do them.
quests.explanation: 'As' here expresses manner - 'the way that'. 'Do exactly as the instructions say' means 'do it in exactly the way that the instructions describe'. This is a distinct use of 'as' separate from time or cause.

quests.question: The whole audience fell silent ____ the conductor raised the baton.
quests.sentence: The whole audience fell silent ____ the conductor raised the baton.
quests.hint: The silence and the raising of the baton happened at the same precise moment.
quests.explanation: 'As' captures simultaneous action with great precision. The moment the baton went up (trigger), the silence fell (response) - both happened at the exact same instant. 'When' is also possible but 'as' conveys the immediacy more vividly.

quests.question: Everyone in the room turned to look at him ____ he walked in late.
quests.sentence: Everyone in the room turned to look at him ____ he walked in late.
quests.hint: His arrival was the specific moment that caused everyone to look.
quests.explanation: 'When' marks the specific moment that triggered the response. The moment he walked in (trigger), everyone looked (reaction). 'While' would imply looking happened during an extended period of walking in.

quests.question: The room grew quieter and quieter ____ the lecture went on longer than expected.
quests.sentence: The room grew quieter and quieter ____ the lecture went on longer than expected.
quests.hint: The quietness increased in proportion to how long the lecture continued - both changed together.
quests.explanation: 'As' expresses parallel, proportional change. 'As the lecture went on' means the room grew quieter at the same rate the lecture extended - two things developing together, not one simply triggering the other.

quests.question: He was daydreaming about his holiday ____ the teacher was explaining the exercise.
quests.sentence: He was daydreaming about his holiday ____ the teacher was explaining the exercise.
quests.hint: Daydreaming and the teacher explaining were two simultaneous activities.
quests.explanation: 'While' connects two activities happening at the same time. He was daydreaming (his mental activity) while the teacher was explaining (the classroom activity) - both were ongoing at the same moment.

quests.question: She knocked the glass off the desk ____ she stood up too quickly.
quests.sentence: She knocked the glass off the desk ____ she stood up too quickly.
quests.hint: Standing up too quickly was the single triggering moment for the accident.
quests.explanation: 'When' marks the specific moment that caused the accident. The glass was knocked off at the exact moment she stood up quickly. 'While' would suggest the knocking happened over an extended period.

quests.question: He grew more and more irritated ____ the long delay dragged on.
quests.sentence: He grew more and more irritated ____ the long delay dragged on.

quests.explanation: 'As' shows gradual, parallel change. His irritation increased proportionally as the delay got longer - both developed together. 'While' is also possible here but 'as' better captures the proportional growth.

quests.question: She felt a huge wave of relief ____ she saw her name on the pass list.
quests.sentence: She felt a huge wave of relief ____ she saw her name on the pass list.

quests.explanation: 'When' marks the specific moment that caused an emotional reaction. The relief came at the exact moment of seeing her name. 'As' could also work, but 'when' is more natural for a single discrete moment.

quests.question: The family dog stretched and yawned ____ everyone was out at work.
quests.sentence: The family dog stretched and yawned ____ everyone was out at work.
quests.hint: The stretching and the family being out both happened during the same period.
quests.explanation: 'While' shows a background condition (family being at work) during which a foreground action (dog stretching) occurred. Both happened over the same time period during the day.

quests.question: He checked his messages ____ he was waiting in the queue at the bank.
quests.sentence: He checked his messages ____ he was waiting in the queue at the bank.
quests.hint: Checking messages and queuing were simultaneous activities.
quests.explanation: 'While' connects two simultaneous activities. He used his phone (active choice) while he was in the queue (background condition) - both happened during the same period of waiting.

quests.question: ____ the pianist began to play, the entire audience fell completely silent.
quests.sentence: ____ the pianist began to play, the entire audience fell completely silent.
quests.hint: The pianist starting and the silence falling happened at the very same instant.
quests.explanation: 'As' introduces perfect simultaneity at the beginning of a sentence. The moment the pianist started (trigger), silence fell (immediate response) - 'as' shows both happened at precisely the same instant.

quests.question: Everyone in the café looked up ____ she walked through the door.
quests.sentence: Everyone in the café looked up ____ she walked through the door.
quests.hint: Her entry through the door was the single moment that caused everyone to look.
quests.explanation: 'When' marks the specific triggering moment. The moment she walked in (trigger), everyone looked up (response). 'As' would be equally correct, but 'when' is more common in everyday usage.

quests.question: She browsed the sale rack ____ she waited for the fitting room to free up.
quests.sentence: She browsed the sale rack ____ she waited for the fitting room to free up.
quests.hint: Browsing and waiting for the fitting room happened at the same time.
quests.explanation: 'While' connects two simultaneous activities. She browsed the sale rack (foreground activity) during the same time she waited for a fitting room (background situation) - both happened together in the shop.

quests.question: He dropped everything and rushed to hospital ____ he heard about the accident.
quests.sentence: He dropped everything and rushed to hospital ____ he heard about the accident.
quests.hint: Hearing about the accident was the precise moment that triggered the rush.
quests.explanation: 'When' marks the specific moment that caused an immediate, urgent reaction. The moment he heard the news (trigger), he rushed to hospital (response). 'As' would also work, but 'when' is more natural for a sudden reaction.

quests.question: The birds began to sing ____ the first light of dawn appeared on the horizon.
quests.sentence: The birds began to sing ____ the first light of dawn appeared on the horizon.
quests.hint: The birdsong and the first light appeared at the very same instant.
quests.explanation: 'As' captures the perfect simultaneity of two natural events. The birds sang at the exact moment the dawn light appeared - both happened simultaneously. 'When' is also possible, but 'as' is preferred for natural, simultaneous events.

quests.question: She was very careful not to make any noise ____ the baby was sleeping.
quests.sentence: She was very careful not to make any noise ____ the baby was sleeping.
quests.hint: She was careful throughout the whole period of the baby's sleep.
quests.explanation: 'While' shows a state maintained for the duration of another ongoing event. She was careful (continuous behaviour) during the whole time the baby was sleeping (background condition).

quests.question: She automatically checks her social media ____ she sits on the bus.
quests.sentence: She automatically checks her social media ____ she sits on the bus.

quests.question: He memorised his presentation notes ____ he was commuting to work.
quests.sentence: He memorised his presentation notes ____ he was commuting to work.

quests.question: She paused for a moment ____ she chose her words very carefully.
quests.sentence: She paused for a moment ____ she chose her words very carefully.

quests.question: The kettle automatically switches itself off ____ the water reaches boiling point.
quests.sentence: The kettle automatically switches itself off ____ the water reaches boiling point.
quests.hint: Reaching boiling point is the precise technical trigger for switching off.
quests.explanation: 'When' marks the specific condition that triggers the automatic response. The kettle switches off at the exact moment the water boils (trigger). This is a mechanical reaction to a specific temperature threshold.

quests.question: She picked up a magazine ____ she waited to see the dentist.
quests.sentence: She picked up a magazine ____ she waited to see the dentist.

quests.explanation: 'While' connects two simultaneous activities. She read the magazine (foreground activity) during the same time she was waiting (background condition) - both happened in the waiting room.

quests.question: He improved steadily and consistently ____ he practised more and more.
quests.sentence: He improved steadily and consistently ____ he practised more and more.
quests.hint: Improvement grew in direct proportion to practice - both developed together.
quests.explanation: 'As' expresses parallel, proportional development. His improvement grew at the same rate as his practice - 'as he practised more' shows the two things increased together. This is the parallel-development use of 'as'.

quests.question: ____ some people prefer quiet evenings at home, others love going out every night.
quests.sentence: ____ some people prefer quiet evenings at home, others love going out every night.
quests.hint: Two contrasting preferences are being compared - this 'while' is used for contrast.
quests.explanation: 'While' can express formal contrast between two different situations or groups, similar to 'whereas'. Here it contrasts two lifestyle preferences. This is different from the temporal use of 'while' - this 'while' means 'on the other hand'.

quests.question: She always double-checks her bag ____ she leaves the house.
quests.sentence: She always double-checks her bag ____ she leaves the house.
quests.hint: Leaving the house is the regular trigger for checking her bag.
quests.explanation: 'When' describes a habitual sequence. Every time she leaves the house (trigger), she checks her bag (habit). 'Before' would also work here, but 'when' is equally natural for a habitual routine.

quests.question: He quietly slipped out of the building ____ the meeting was still going on.
quests.sentence: He quietly slipped out of the building ____ the meeting was still going on.
quests.hint: Slipping out and the meeting continuing were simultaneous - he left during it.
quests.explanation: 'As' shows the two things happening at the same time, with one providing the background for the other. He left (foreground action) while the meeting continued (background condition) - 'as' captures this perfectly.
